main_issue: Whether and when the small room can be reserved for Agent D's daily prayers (about 1:15 and 3:30) without clashing with others' needs

A-B.evidence: A and B each state their own constraints (turns 3-4) and never address each other. B's file-moving plan (17) is not rejected by A, but A never explicitly endorses it, so alignment stays modest.

A-C.evidence: A and C raise separate constraints (turns 1, 5) and do not speak to each other. At the end both are accommodated by D's times and C approves B's plan (18).

A-D.evidence: A rejects the 4:30 slot (1, 3) and D moves to 4:00, 3:45, then 3:30 (2, 8, 15); A: '3:30 works. Thanks.' (16)

B-C.evidence: C responds to B's idea of moving the files: 'That sounds like a good solution.' (18)

B-D.evidence: B worries about file access (9, 12) and D says they can't be interrupted (13). B proposes moving the files (17) and D agrees: 'Yes, that works.' (21)

C-D.evidence: C says 1 p.m. is a problem (5). C offers 'you could have the room from 1:15' (7) and D accepts (8).
